evals.prompt: The owner starts an approved Jig phase with three ready stories and already-assigned semantic implementer/reviewer pairs. One story is bounded, directly specified, local, and has straightforward positive/negative proof. A GF-020-like story would add public identity, durable ledger authority, and policy fields but no exact source authorizes those public semantics; package-private bookkeeping is separately and clearly authorized. A GF-022-like story requires exact bytes, restart recovery, retry lineage, and deadline integrity. Offload plans the two risky implementations on Luna/high. It separately plans every semantic reviewer on Terra/high through a compatible configurable runtime type, with isolated context, a hard budget, and a provider fallback policy that preserves high effort and records planned and actual routes separately. A fixed Codex implementer runtime type would instead force the Terra model at medium effort, and the provider explicitly reports Luna unavailable for the exact-bytes story. Describe risk classification, pre-write preparation, dispatch, fallback, authority handling, and admission.
evals.expected_output: Treat global offload as an orchestration prerequisite and stop before admission with a missing-dependency error if it is unavailable; do not invent a local route, lower effort, or return OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED for that operational gap. Keep the genuinely local story eligible for medium, but require high for both authority/identity and exact-bytes/recovery/retry/deadline work regardless of file count. Treat implementer/reviewer as semantic ownership roles, use global offload to plan each implementer and reviewer role's model, effort, compatible runtime type, isolated context, budget, and fallback routing, have Jig assign and record verification ownership in the dispatch trace, and reject the fixed Codex implementer runtime type because it forces the incompatible Terra model at medium effort instead of the planned Luna model at high effort. Begin no writes until the accepted spawn preserves the route. For explicit Luna unavailability, retain Luna as planned_model, use Terra as actual_model at high effort, and record model_unavailable. Preserve each reviewer's explicit Terra/high plan, isolated context, hard budget, and same-effort planned/actual fallback accounting. The reviewer prepares stable-ID must-cover bullets plus an authority result before writes: the GF-020-like story returns OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED and all of its writes, including otherwise authorized package-private bookkeeping, remain stopped until authority is resolved or the owner explicitly reauthorizes a narrower story scope. Continue independent ready stories and add no agent, artifact, approval, or ledger field.
assertions: Keeps medium eligible only for the directly specified local story with local effects and straightforward positive and negative proof
Requires high for GF-020-like authority and identity semantics and GF-022-like exact bytes, recovery, retry, and deadline semantics regardless of file count
Treats implementer and reviewer as semantic roles that do not choose runtime agent types
Treats global offload as a required orchestration dependency and stops before story admission without weakening routing when it is unavailable

Uses offload to resolve explicit model, effort, compatible runtime type, isolated context, budget, and fallback routing for every implementer and reviewer while Jig assigns and records verification ownership in the dispatch trace

Rejects the fixed Codex implementer runtime type because it forces the incompatible Terra model at medium effort instead of the planned Luna model at high effort and begins no writes on that mismatched route
Preserves Luna as planned model and high effort while recording Terra as actual model with model_unavailable only after explicit provider unavailability
Requires stable-ID must-cover preparation and an authority-boundary result before writes
Returns OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED for the mixed-authority story and blocks all of that story's writes until authority is resolved or the owner explicitly reauthorizes a narrower scope
Continues independent ready stories without adding an agent, artifact, approval stage, tracked dispatch artifact, or ledger field

evals.prompt: A Jig implementer receives eight stable-ID must-cover bullets. Its handoff names concrete code and tests for five, says only 'covered' for two hostile-input and recovery bullets, and omits the sibling-operation bullet. The implementation owner has not yet run the candidate checks. After the handoff is repaired and owner-run evidence is recorded, the read-only reviewer inspects the exact candidate, accidentally reruns git diff --check once, and finds one local blocker plus one structural root cause affecting several sibling types. Describe candidate state, required proof mapping, reviewer recovery and input/output, and the correction path.
evals.expected_output: Keep the story implementing: every must-cover ID needs concrete implementation and applicable type/test locations or a justified non-testable designation, sibling-search scope/result, and implementation-owner verification evidence; 'covered' and omission cannot freeze a candidate. One test may prove multiple bullets, but hostile, negative, adversarial, and recovery requirements need their applicable proof. After the complete mapping and owner-run checks produce a committed candidate, give the reviewer the exact candidate/diff, authority, bullets, proof mapping, recorded evidence, prior findings, and incremental range. Discard the reviewer's prohibited git diff --check run as review evidence and reissue the bounded review to the same reviewer. The reviewer consumes recorded checks, completes the presently supportable pass, returns PASS or CHANGES_REQUIRED, groups every blocker by root cause with source/invariant, affected sibling surface, evidence gaps, and exact re-review scope. A false mapping is CHANGES_REQUIRED; local defects use the same-pair loop, while structural defects first restate the corrected realization before changes and full owner verification.
assertions: Keeps the story implementing when any must-cover ID is omitted or supported only by a generic coverage claim
Requires concrete implementation, applicable type and test proof or justified non-testable status, sibling-search scope and result, and owner-run verification evidence for every must-cover ID
Allows one test to prove multiple bullets without weakening hostile, negative, adversarial, recovery, or sibling proof
Requires implementation-owner checks before candidate freeze and gives their recorded evidence to the reviewer
Requires exact candidate, authority, bullets, proof mapping, prior findings, and exact incremental range as reviewer input
Discards a one-off prohibited non-mutating reviewer check as evidence and reissues the bounded review to the same reviewer
Requires a complete review pass with all supportable blockers grouped by root cause, source or invariant, affected siblings, evidence gaps, and exact re-review scope
Treats false or inadequate proof mapping as CHANGES_REQUIRED
Keeps local defects in the same-pair loop and requires a structural realization restatement before code changes and owner-run verification

evals.prompt: During a Jig story correction, the implementer first returns an incomplete patch with concrete code/test progress, then later produces two consecutive turns with no concrete progress. In another branch of the scenario, the same root semantic defect survives two correction candidates, the exceptional replacement reproduces it, and the reviewer repeats a prohibited check after an earlier corrected reminder. Separately, recover a ledger-listed worktree when its exact branch/object reconciles cleanly, when the object is missing, and when the surviving workspace is dirty or mismatched. Describe continuity, replacement/stop behavior, recovery, and whether a fresh clone is allowed.
evals.expected_output: Keep the advancing implementer and same reviewer; incompleteness alone is not replacement. Permit exceptional implementer replacement only after the two consecutive no-progress turns or after the same root defect survives two correction candidates, recording the existing reason and handoff. If the replacement reproduces that defect, stop the affected story under existing execution-blocking rules instead of spawning another chain. Replace the reviewer after the repeated boundary breach, while a single prohibited non-mutating check would only have its evidence discarded and the same bounded review reissued; mutation, evidence writing, unavailability, or an incompatible runtime route are also exceptional replacement causes. If the replacement reviewer repeats the same qualifying boundary, mutation, evidence-writing, or availability failure, stop the affected story under existing execution-blocking rules rather than replacing again. For worktree recovery, reconcile git worktree list, reattach only the exact clean recorded branch/object at its registered path, block the affected story for missing/dirty/mismatched facts while independent stories continue, use OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED only for a material authority decision, and reject a fresh local clone.
assertions: Retains an incomplete implementer when the turn contains concrete code or test progress
Allows exceptional implementer replacement after two consecutive no-progress turns or the same root semantic defect survives two correction candidates
Stops the affected story instead of creating an unbounded chain when the replacement reproduces the same root defect
Replaces a reviewer only after a repeated boundary breach or immediate mutation, evidence writing, or loss of availability
Stops the affected story instead of creating another reviewer replacement chain when the replacement repeats the same qualifying failure
Treats an incompatible approved runtime route as an exceptional replacement cause without lowering the planned route
Records replacement using the existing reason and handoff rather than adding schema
Starts worktree recovery with git worktree list reconciliation and reattaches only the exact clean recorded branch and object at the registered path
Blocks only the affected story and descendants for missing objects or dirty and mismatched evidence while independent ready stories continue
Uses OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED only for a material authority decision and rejects fresh-clone recovery
